coverageSpotVerification.detail: The manifest maps exactly the suite-required set of every milestone in scope (7+22+7+5+6+5+6 = 58 mappings; the frozen validator at instrument/metering/coverage-manifest.mjs re-validated it green on my own suite invocation, sha256 ffe76ccd63a9d2bd9e72202cd1e10a28e4a9d7af8eebc548a4a680d96dd057d4). I read every mapped test in scripts/acceptance*.mjs and checked that it exercises the assertion's observable, then re-executed each sampled observable myself. No mapping is fabricated or no-opped; several are stronger than required (m3-a11 measures the jumped-to bubble's bounding rect; m3-a15 diffs full per-conversation message-id lists; m4-a10 waits the real 61 s window; m5-a01..a03 wait real expiry with every client closed). Verdict honest. Two mappings are incomplete rather than dishonest, and I exercised the unexercised clause in each - both pass: (1) m1-a08's mapped test 'profile fields persist' asserts only the bio clause, never reading back the display name, although the save does write it; my API check confirms both clauses persist. (2) m8-a05 ('ranks the post with the most likes first') maps to a test whose two Trending posts carry EQUAL like counts, so ordering by like count is never differentially exercised - only the tie-break is; on an isolated instance with 3/2/1 likes I confirmed strict like-count ordering. A third, narrower note: m1-a03's mapped test exercises duplicate-handle rejection at profile save rather than at signup, which is the only place a handle exists in this app's flow (signup is email+password per the brief's spec) - a correct reading, not a gap. No milestone is adjudicated to capability-failure.

defects.summary: On a freshly loaded web client the first profile-save mutation is refused with the platform's internal message 'the backend store is not identified yet; mutation was not admitted' instead of being deferred until the replica has identified its store, and the form then stays stuck (a second save on the same mounted form is refused identically) until the route is re-navigated. Reproducible 3 of 3 with no settle delay and 0 of 3 with a >=1.5 s delay. Two consequences beyond the checklist: the visible error in a duplicate-handle attempt is this internal diagnostic rather than a handle error, and the lane's own gate is destabilised - my first `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m1` failed exactly here and the frozen choreography's profile-edit-live-visibility assertion failed 2 of its 3 attempts with outcomeClass 'application' before passing in 167 ms.

Sender avatars in conversation bubbles never render the sender's uploaded avatar image; they fall back permanently to the kit's initials placeholder (and rendered with no initials text at all in group bubbles). Measured: 20 of 20 sender-avatar nodes in a DM are fallback DIVs with zero loaded images after 30 s of settling, and 0 of 2 in a group, while on the same page load the same users' avatars render as 20 of 20 fully painted elements in the feed and their avatar assets resolve normally over the API. The identity and accessible label are correct, so this is an asset-resolution failure in the message-bubble component (useAsset(author?.avatar?.id) never reaches 'ready'), not a missing node. The frozen harness never adjudicated this because its avatar check is gated on finding the node in its own flow and it recorded a skip with outcomeClass 'instrument'.

The documented acceptance entrypoint silently depends on a separately started effects worker. `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m6` fails m6-a08 and m6-a09 after a 90 s wait with 'Push payload not delivered within 90 seconds' when `node scripts/start-worker.mjs` is not already running; the message names neither the worker nor the log it is polling, and the suite neither starts nor checks for the seam it depends on. With the worker started (as README documents) all four M6 tests pass. Cost me one wasted suite cycle and would mislead anyone reproducing the lane.

Thin margins on live two-client updates: 6 of the 44 recorded choreography attempts failed and were rescued by best-of-3 - profile-edit-live-visibility 2 of 3, feed-image-post-live-update 1 of 3, feed-video-post-live-update 1 of 3, quoted-reply-excerpt-and-jump 2 of 3, photo-message-live-render 1 of 3, reaction-live-replace-remove 1 of 3. The profile-edit pair is explained by d-01; the rest are timeouts on a shared machine, absorbed by the frozen best-of-3 rule and so not scored as failures, but recorded because the passing attempts sit within a few seconds of the harness's observation windows.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts').
O1.justification: 100 of the 119 frozen assertions pass under my independent execution and exactly one fails (m3-a02, defect d-02); there is no milestone that is merely patchy. Every milestone the run attempted is green on both legs - a coverage-validated suite run (I re-ran all seven suites myself; 58 mapped assertions, zero missing) and a passing web choreography segment. That puts the run far past the 60 anchor. It stops short of 90 on the anchor's own two clauses. First, 'every in-scope milestone': M7 contributes 0 of 9, never attempted because ENVIRONMENT.md reserves it for a separate later session, and O1's rule keeps it in the denominator regardless of status. Second, 'including platform-proof artifacts': the iOS Hermes bundle export exists for all seven milestones, but the separately recorded iOS simulator artifact does not exist for either M6 or M8, so the nine native-artifact assertions (m6-a01..a07, m8-a17, m8-a18) record no proof of any kind and the whole cold-start-offline group is unevidenced. Quality of the passing work is high rather than nominal: my own re-execution reproduced every observable, including clauses the lane's suite covers only weakly (display-name persistence, Trending's like-count ordering with unequal counts, the server asset endpoint after delete, grouped-search contiguity), and found no wrong data anywhere.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), held near 60 by two major defects.
O2.justification: Two major defects, one minor and one cosmetic, against a wide search that found nothing worse. d-01 is a genuine core-flow race: the first profile-save on a cold client is refused with an internal platform diagnostic and the form stays stuck until re-navigation - on the happy path, reproducible 3 of 3, and it destabilised the lane's own gate. d-02 is a specced surface silently degraded: message bubbles never load the sender's uploaded avatar, 0 of 20 in a DM, while the feed's avatars load 20 of 20 on the same page. Against that, the breadth of what held up is the reason this is not below 60: a 13-probe cross-principal sweep found no authorization hole (non-member reads of history, message-by-id, roster, in-chat search, global search and the public custom-client API are all denied; non-member send/seen/react and non-owner edit/delete are all refused server-side; a handle cannot be taken), the server asset endpoint is bearer-scoped and stops serving on delete, view-once and expiry are enforced server-side with every client closed, like/repost set-state is idempotent under repeats and replayed write ids, feed pagination produced no duplicates and no gaps over 24 fresh posts in both tabs, the seed is byte-identically idempotent, and the digest counts matched authored activity exactly including across a mid-period backend restart. No crash, no data loss and no wrong count was observed in any probe.
